articles.title: 'I'm proud of it': Killer confesses after murdering Ian Huntley
articles.summary: Triple murderer Anthony Russell said he planned to kill Ian Huntley and that he had "nothing to lose".
articles.body:
A triple murderer who beat the notorious child-killer Ian Huntley to death in prison has been given a second whole life jail term.

Anthony Russell, 44, repeatedly bludgeoned Huntley, 52, with a metal bar at the high security Frankland Prison near Durham in February, Newcastle Crown Court heard.

In footage released by the Crown Prosecution Service, Russell confesses to planning to kill Huntley and says: "I'm proud of it."

Russell, who was jailed for life with no chance of parole in March 2022 for raping and murdering a pregnant woman and killing a mother and son in the West Midlands, admitted Huntley's murder on the second day of his trial.

Sentencing him for what prosecutors called a "cold-blooded" and planned attack , Mr Justice Hilliard KC said Russell would never be freed from prison or eligible for parole.

Huntley was serving a life sentence at the high security Frankland jail for murdering Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman in Soham, Cambridgeshire, in 2002.

articles.title: Temporal em Sapucaia: Sobe para 23 o número de desalojados | G1
articles.standfirst: Pessoas atingidas estão abrigadas em casas de familiares. Prefeitura iniciou uma campanha para arrecadar doações de roupas, móveis e roupas de cama.
articles.summary: Com 23 desalojados após temporal em Sapucaia, prefeitura arrecada doações de móveis e roupas para famílias atingidas pela chuva de 120mm no distrito de Anta.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Subiu para 23 o número de pessoas desalojadas após o temporal que atingiu Sapucaia (RJ) na noite de segunda-feira (23). O novo balanço foi divulgado pela prefeitura na tarde desta terça-feira (24).

Segundo o governo municipal, os desalojados são moradores de dez imóveis no distrito de Anta. Deste total, 22 pessoas moram na Rua Ana de Jesus Mendonça e uma na Rua José Leopoldo Guimarães.

Entre os desalojados, estão quatro idosos, duas crianças e um adolescente. Todos tiveram as casas invadidas pela água da chuva e foram para residências de familiares. As famílias estão recebendo atendimento da assistência social.

Temporal deixa família desalojada, provoca enxurradas e destrói ruas em Sapucaia — Foto: Divulgação/Redes Sociais

A Prefeitura de Sapucaia iniciou uma campanha para arrecadar doações destinadas aos moradores atingidos pelo temporal.

As doações devem ser entregues nos Centros de Referência de Assistência Social (Cras) do município.

Segundo um novo balanço divulgado pela prefeitura, choveu mais de 120 milímetros em menos de uma hora. Inicialmente, a Defesa Civil havia estimado que o volume de chuva tivesse chegado a aproximadamente 100 milímetros.

O pluviômetro, equipamento utilizado para medir o volume de chuva, registrou 20,83 milímetros antes de apresentar uma falha durante o temporal. A suspeita é de que o problema tenha sido causado por falta de conexão com a internet ou danos no aparelho.

Na Rua Campo Alegre, a força da enxurrada arrancou paralelepípedos e destruiu parte do calçamento. A correnteza também arrastou um carro, que só parou após bater contra um caminhão estacionado.

Equipes de diferentes secretarias municipais estão trabalhando em vários pontos da cidade, principalmente no distrito de Anta, um dos mais atingidos pelo temporal.

articles.title: Tirolesa gratuita: veja como participar e quem pode andar em RO | G1

articles.summary: A tirolesa em Porto Velho funciona gratuitamente no Parque da Cidade até janeiro, exigindo idade mínima de 7 anos e check-in diário realizado pelo aplicativo PVH+.

Quem quiser andar de tirolesa durante a programação de Natal em Porto Velho poderá aproveitar a atração gratuitamente no Parque da Cidade. A atividade começa no dia 28 de novembro e ficará disponível até 10 de janeiro de 2027.

As informações sobre o funcionamento foram divulgadas pela Prefeitura de Porto Velho. A estrutura contará com equipamentos de segurança e acompanhamento de monitores durante todo o percurso.

Para utilizar a atração, é necessário acessar o aplicativo PVH+ e realizar o check-in na atividade. O procedimento deve ser feito no próprio dia da visita ao Parque da Cidade.

O atendimento será realizado por ordem de chegada e não será necessário pagar para andar na tirolesa. A atração funcionará diariamente, das 16h15 às 22h.

Tirolesa gratuita em Porto Velho — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Porto Velho

A tirolesa estará disponível para pessoas com idade mínima de 7 anos.

Os equipamentos de segurança serão fornecidos no próprio local e deverão ser utilizados obrigatoriamente por todos os participantes. Monitores capacitados também estarão no espaço para orientar e acompanhar as pessoas durante a atividade.

Em caso de chuva, a tirolesa será suspensa temporariamente . A atividade só poderá funcionar novamente quando houver condições consideradas seguras para os participantes.

articles.title: Criminosos fazem reféns em supermercado em Cartagena | G1
articles.standfirst: Episódio mobilizou operação policial de larga escala e ocorre em meio à principal onda de violência no país latino-americano nos últimos anos. Acordo de paz entre governo e Farc completou dez anos nesta terça-feira (24).
articles.summary: Episódio mobilizou operação policial de larga escala e ocorre em meio à principal onda de violência recente no país. Acordo de paz entre governo e Farc completou 10 anos.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Dois criminosos fazem 24 pessoas reféns nesta terça-feira (24) em um supermercado na cidade turística de Cartagena, na Colômbia .

Mais cedo, cinco mulheres idosas, que estavam entre os cativos, foram libertadas. Um homem também foi liberado em meio às negociaões da polícia com os bandidos. Não há nenhum ferido , segundo a imprensa local.

O episódio fez o presidente do país, Abelardo de la Espriella, mobilizar as principais forças policiais colombianas e reacendeu temores da volta de uma onda de violência no país.

➡️ Na noite de segunda-feira (23), um carro-bomba explodiu na cidade de Villavicencio, na região central da Colômbia . Ainda não havia informação, até a última atualização desta reportagem, de ligação entre os dois episódios, que ocorrem exatos dez anos após o acordo de paz entre as Farc e o governo colombiano .

Polícia colombiana se concentra em frente a supermercado em Cartagena, na Colômbia, onde criminosos fizeram dezenas de reféns, em 24 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Alexander Urzola Cuadrado/ Reuters

Policiais e atiradores de elite foram posicionados em prédios nos arredores do estabelecimento. Dentro do supermercado, era possível ver indivíduos encapuzados portando armas longas ao lado dos reféns .

Segundo o jornal colombiano El Tiempo, os suspeitos tentavam assaltar o estabelecimento por voltas das 8h no horário local (10h na hora de Brasília), quando a polícia chegou. Diante dos agentes, eles se trancaram no mercado junto dos clientes e permaneciam no local até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Por conta do episódio, as chegadas de voos no aeroporto de Cartagena, a cidade mais famosa do Caribe colombiano, chegaram a ser suspensas , mas já foram reativadas, segundo a agência de aviação do país.

Segundo o jornal espanhol "El País", os sequestradores exigem cerca de 7 bilhões de pesos colombianos (cerca de R$ 9,5 milhões) e livre passagem para seguir rumo a Barranquilla, a 130 km de Cartagena.

"Todas as capacidades das nossas diversas forças de segurança foram agora mobilizadas, incluindo unidades especiais", disse Espriella.

Homens do Grupo de Operações Especiais da Polícia da Colômbia chegam a supermercado onde criminosos fizeram dezenas de reféns em Cartagena, em 24 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Alexander Urzola Cuadrado/ Reuters

Mulher é amparada por policial após ser libertada de supermercado em Cartagena, Colômbia, onde bandidos fizeram dezenas de pessoas reféns, em 24 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Alexander Urzola Cuadrado/ Reuters

👉 O sequestro ocorre no mesmo dia em que se completa o décimo aniversário do histórico acordo de paz de 2016 que desarmou a guerrilha das Farc, e em meio à pior onda de violência no país desde então.

Desde que chegou ao poder, neste ano, Abelardo de la Espriella vem promovendo uma política de linha dura contra os criminosos, com bombardeios letais e operações policiais. No entanto, a violência no país não deu sinais de diminuição nos últimos meses.

Mesmo após a assinatura do acordo de paz há uma década, grupos ilegais disputam rotas de tráfico de drogas e áreas de mineração ilegal, alimentando o terror no país com sequestros e atentados.

Na noite de segunda-feira, uma dissidência da guerrilha das Farc detonou um carro-bomba na cidade de Villavicencio, deixando 25 feridos e graves destruições. Espriella acusou a principal dissidência das Farc pelo atentado .

articles.title: Acidente em Ouro Fino: Cantor Zeno Capato Filho morre em rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na tarde desta terça-feira (24), no bairro Cervinho, em Ouro Fino (MG); equipes de resgate, polícia e perícia foram acionadas.
articles.summary: O cantor Zeno Capato Filho e seu ajudante morreram após o caminhão da banda cair em um rio em Ouro Fino; a suspeita é de falha mecânica no veículo.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Duas pessoas morreram após o caminhão em que estavam cair dentro de um rio próximo a uma ponte na tarde desta terça-feira (24) no bairro Cervinho, zona rural de Ouro Fino , no Sul de Minas. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o acidente aconteceu por volta de 13h.

Segundo a Polícia Militar, o local do acidente fica entre a zona urbana de Ouro Fino e a zona rural de Borda da Mata. A suspeita é que o caminhão, que estava carregado de equipamentos e instrumentos musicais, tenha sofrido uma falha mecânica e o condutor tenha perdido o controle da direção, saindo da pista e caindo no Rio Cervo.

Cantor e ajudante morrem após caminhão cair em rio na zona rural de Ouro Fino, MG — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Segundo apuração da EPTV, as vítimas são o cantor Zeno Capato Filho, de 67 anos, integrante da Aphocalipse Banda Show, de Artur Nogueira (SP) e o ajudante do músico, Juliano Lucas, conhecido como "Pezão", de 48 anos. A informação foi confirmada pela vocalista Vanusa Santos, integrante da banda. Ainda segundo a vocalista, os dois estavam no trecho de Borda da Mata com destino a Santa Rita de Caldas.

Cantor de música country e ajudante morrem após caminhão cair em rio na zona rural em MG — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Ainda segundo a vocalista, os dois estavam no trecho de Borda da Mata com destino a Santa Rita de Caldas.

A vocalista Vanusa Santos e o cantor Zeno Capato Filho, da Aphocalipse Banda Show — Foto: Reprodução / Redes Sociais

Nas redes sociais, a organização da "Calvada em Crisólia", distrito de Ouro Fino (MG), lamentou a morte do músico e do ajudante: "Em 2024, realizamos um sonho: trazer a banda Aphocalypse para abrilhantar nossa Cavalgada de Crisólia, em uma edição que foi um grande sucesso e ficará para sempre em nossa memória. Infelizmente hoje recebemos a triste notícia do falecimento de nossos amigos Zeno e Pezão".

Segundo a funerária responsável, os corpos foram levados para o IML de Pouso Alegre. Até a publicação desta reportagem, o caminhão permanecia no Rio Cervo.

articles.title: Saquarema recebe evento com consultorias gratuitas para pequenos negócios  | G1
articles.standfirst: Movimenta Sebrae acontece de 26 a 28 de novembro, com palestras, oficinas, orientação financeira e atividades para quem tem ou pretende abrir uma empresa.
articles.summary: Movimenta Sebrae acontece de 26 a 28 de novembro, com palestras, oficinas, orientação financeira e atividades para quem tem ou pretende abrir uma empresa.
articles.body:

Como organizar as contas de uma empresa? De que forma a inteligência artificial pode ajudar nas vendas? O que é preciso saber antes de abrir o próprio negócio? O Movimenta Sebrae que chega a Saquarema nesta quinta-feira (26) vai trazer muita informação e conteúdo para a região.

A iniciativa, que vem percorrendo diferentes municípios do estado do Rio de Janeiro, integra a programação do Conecta Saquarema e acontece até sábado (28), das 14h às 21h, no Centro de Eventos de Saquarema, em Porto da Roça. A participação é gratuita e as inscrições podem ser feitas pela internet.

Durante os três dias, profissionais do Sebrae Rio estarão à disposição de empreendedores de toda a Região dos Lagos para consultorias e orientações sobre negócios. A programação atende tanto quem já possui uma empresa quanto quem ainda está planejando empreender.

Prepare-se para sua empresa ir mais longe. Participe! — Foto: Divulgação

Região dos Lagos reúne mais de 116 mil pequenos negócios

De acordo com dados do Sebrae Rio, a Região dos Lagos concentra 116,5 mil pequenos negócios. Desse total, 73,9 mil são microempreendedores individuais (MEIs), 37,8 mil são microempresas e 4,7 mil são empresas de pequeno porte.

O setor de serviços responde por 46,56% desses empreendimentos, seguido pelo comércio, com 26,67%, e pela indústria, com 16,13%. Turismo, economia criativa e agropecuária também fazem parte desse cenário.

Em todo o estado do Rio de Janeiro, são mais de dois milhões de pequenos negócios.

Parte da programação em Saquarema será dedicada justamente às dificuldades enfrentadas por esses empresários no cotidiano, como a administração das finanças, a divulgação de produtos e serviços, o relacionamento com clientes e a busca por novos mercados.

“Os pequenos negócios são fundamentais para a economia da Região dos Lagos, movimentam o comércio, os serviços, o turismo e geram oportunidades em diferentes municípios. O Movimenta Sebrae foi pensado justamente para oferecer aos empreendedores acesso a conhecimento, ferramentas de gestão, inovação e conexões que possam fazer a diferença no dia a dia de suas empresas. Queremos que eles aproveitem essa oportunidade para ampliar seus horizontes, trocar experiências e identificar novos caminhos para crescer”, afirma Ana Claudia Vieira, coordenadora do Sebrae Rio na Região dos Lagos.

Da inteligência artificial à educação financeira

O uso da tecnologia na gestão de restaurantes, as mudanças no comportamento das novas gerações e a organização financeira das empresas estão entre os assuntos que serão discutidos no auditório principal do evento.

A programação reúne nomes como Ro Gouvêa, que vai tratar de “Gestão gastronômica na era da IA”; Dado Schneider, que vai apresentar a palestra “Não é idade, é mentalidade: o choque de realidade das novas gerações”; Bruno UAU abordando “Gente feliz dá lucro… e não enche o saco”; Teco Medina, com “Educação Financeira para pequenos negócios”; Luciano Potter, e “Tenha amigos e fique rico”; além de Marcus Macedo, que trará o “Panorama regional: maturidade, potencialidades e oportunidades para os negócios”, entre outros.

O público poderá acompanhar palestras sobre gestão gastronômica na era da inteligência artificial, educação financeira para pequenos negócios, comportamento profissional, relações interpessoais e perspectivas para a economia regional.

Quem procura fornecedores, clientes ou parceiros comerciais também poderá participar da Sessão de Negócios, atividade voltada à aproximação entre empresas.

Já no Espaço Inove, o Sebrae Conexões Financeiras vai abordar questões relacionadas à gestão dos recursos das empresas e apresentar soluções financeiras para os pequenos negócios.

Como transformar as redes sociais em ferramentas de trabalho

Para quem vende pela internet ou pretende ampliar a presença da empresa nas redes sociais, uma das atrações será o Espaço Influenciadores. O ambiente terá atividades voltadas à produção de conteúdo digital.

A programação inclui ainda oficinas, experiências imersivas e um Escape Room, atividade interativa em que os participantes precisam solucionar desafios.

Entre as novidades desta edição estão o Espaço Empretec, que apresenta uma metodologia voltada ao desenvolvimento do comportamento empreendedor, e o Espaço Autores, dedicado à produção literária e à troca de conhecimentos.

Produtos da Região dos Lagos ganham espaço

O público também poderá conhecer o trabalho de empreendedores locais no Empório Sebrae e no Shopping MEI, que vão reunir produtos de pequenos negócios da região.

A identidade regional estará presente ainda no Espaço Origens, com apresentações que valorizam a produção local.

Como participar e receber atendimento gratuito

As inscrições para o Movimenta Sebrae estão disponíveis no site oficial do Sebrae Rio. Na página, também é possível consultar a programação do evento.

Quem busca orientação para abrir uma empresa, melhorar a gestão de um negócio ou esclarecer dúvidas sobre empreendedorismo poderá procurar a equipe do Sebrae no local, durante os três dias de realização do evento.

A participação é aberta a moradores de Saquarema e dos demais municípios da Região dos Lagos.

articles.title: Espanha contesta lei regional de Madri que amplia direitos dos fetos | G1
articles.standfirst: Para ministra, conceder direitos legais a um feto é incompatível com a legislação espanhola e poderia enfraquecer o direito ao aborto. Contestação ocorre dias antes das eleições antecipadas no país europeu, marcadas para o próximo domingo (29).
articles.summary: Para ministra, conceder direitos legais a um feto é incompatível com a legislação espanhola e poderia enfraquecer o direito ao aborto. Contestação ocorre dias antes das eleições antecipadas no país europeu, marcadas para o próximo domingo (29).
articles.body:
O primeiro-ministro espanhol, Pedro Sánchez, discursa durante uma coletiva de imprensa após participar de uma cúpula especial de líderes da União Europeia — Foto: REUTERS/Yves Herman

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O governo da Espanha afirmou nesta terça-feira (24) que vai contestar no Tribunal Constitucional uma lei local aprovada na região de Madri que concede direitos a fetos. O embate expõe as divergências entre as políticas sociais dos partidos às vésperas das eleições nacionais antecipadas, marcadas para o próximo domingo (29).

Em junho, o governo regional de centro-direita da capital Madri aprovou uma lei, válida apenas na região, que inclui fetos entre os beneficiários de determinadas medidas, como benefícios fiscais e subsídios destinados a famílias numerosas. O governo espanhol, de Pedro Sánchez , é de esquerda.

A ministra da Igualdade, Ana Redondo, afirmou em entrevista coletiva em Madri que conceder direitos legais a um feto é incompatível com a legislação espanhola e poderia enfraquecer o direito ao aborto.

“Acreditamos que há um conflito entre o direito da mulher de interromper livremente uma gravidez e a lei relativa à criança ainda não nascida”, disse Redondo.

A proposta faz parte do programa eleitoral do conservador Partido Popular (PP) para as eleições de 29 de novembro. O PP lidera a maioria das pesquisas e pode ficar em posição de formar uma maioria após a eleição, em aliança com o partido de extrema direita Vox.

Os socialistas prometeram reforçar ainda mais o direito ao aborto depois que o governo de coalizão minoritário que lideram não conseguiu, durante a atual legislatura, cumprir a promessa de transformar o aborto em um direito constitucional.

Nesta terça-feira, o governo também aprovou um decreto destinado a padronizar o acesso aos serviços de aborto, estabelecendo regras comuns em todo o país para os procedimentos de consentimento informado. O decreto também uniformiza os comitês clínicos responsáveis por autorizar abortos por razões médicas após 14 semanas de gestação.

A Espanha registrou 107.824 abortos em 2025 , uma alta de 1,6%, segundo dados do Ministério da Saúde divulgados nesta terça. Cerca de 6,6% foram realizados por razões médicas.

Como parte de uma série de medidas sociais anunciadas às vésperas da eleição, o governo também aprovou um decreto que amplia para 10 dias úteis a licença por luto após a morte de um familiar e aumenta para 20 semanas a licença parental remunerada.

articles.title: RJ: Dupla é presa por suspeita de tráfico internacional de bebê | G1
articles.standfirst: Os suspeitos foram identificados como Kelly Lee Squire e Qian Gao; investigação apura esquema em que mulheres tailandesas chegam ao Brasil para dar à luz e entregar os bebês a famílias contratantes mediante pagamento.
articles.summary: Os suspeitos foram identificados como Kelly Lee Squire e Qian Gao; investigação apura esquema em que mulheres tailandesas chegam ao Brasil para dar à luz e entregam os bebês.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Um neozelandês e uma chinesa foram presos em flagrante, nesta terça-feira (24), em Saquarema , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, suspeitos de integrar um esquema de tráfico internacional de pessoas, depois que, segundo a Polícia Civil, duas tailandesas deram à luz em um hospital do município.

Foi a unidade de saúde que acionou a polícia ao desconfiar dos nascimentos, meses após outra estrangeira ter feito um parto na unidade. As tailandesas foram ouvidas e, segundo o delegado Vilson de Almeida, estão sendo acompanhadas junto aos bebês pela Assistência Social.

Já o neozelandês, Kelly Lee Squire, e a chinesa Qian Gao, foram presos na própria residência, no bairro Jardim, em Saquarema. De acordo com a investigação, eles atuavam na logística de um esquema que intermediava nascimentos no Brasil e o encaminhamento dos bebês para o exterior.

A Polícia Civil informou que as gestantes receberiam, cada uma, o valor de 700.000 baht (moeda tailandesa), que, convertido em real, equivale a R$ 121.632,00.

"O hospital começou a desconfiar de muitos partos de estrangeiras acontecendo na unidade. Nós desconfiamos e fomos investigar. Iremos atrás de outros integrantes do grupo", disse o delegado titular da 124ª Delegacia de Polícia, Vilson de Almeida.

Neozelandês e chinesa foram presos em Saquarema suspeitos de intermediar tráfico de bebês — Foto: Polícia Civil

Após o comunicado do hospital, as mulheres com os bebês, que têm dias de vida, passaram a ser monitoradas pela Polícia Civil. Foi assim que os agentes, após montar campana na unidade hospitalar, chegaram ao endereço onde o casal foi preso.

As investigações apontam que as tailandesas chegaram ao Brasil já no fim da gestação. A principal linha de investigação é de que elas haviam sido contratadas para gerar crianças para famílias chinesas por meio de acordos de gestação por substituição, prática popularmente conhecida como "barriga de aluguel", que, segundo os investigadores, é proibida na China e na Tailândia.

O delegado Vilson de Almeida acredita que os embriões eram fecundados com material genético dos pais biológicos chineses e implantados nas gestantes tailandesas.

Próximo ao parto, as mulheres eram trazidas ao Brasil, tendo transporte, hospedagem e acompanhamento médico intermediado pelo casal.

A Polícia Civil disse que, ao chegar no Brasil, a gestante consegue atendimento médico no Sistema Único de Saúde.

"Após o nascimento, o pai biológico chinês viaja ao país para realizar o registro da criança, constando como pai, e a gestante tailandesa, como mãe", disse o delegado.

Ainda segundo a Polícia Civil, com a certidão de nascimento, a criança pode sair do Brasil.

"Pode pegar um voo internacional. Aí elas vão embora, só com a certidão de nascimento da criança aqui. É uma cidadã brasileira, nascida no território nacional, um brasileiro nato, que sai do país, e, quando chega lá fora, é dada para a família contratante da barriga de aluguel, e essa criança desaparece, toma destido ignorado com a família", explicou um agente que participou da operação.

"Lá, eles mudam certidão, mudam o registro, não sabemos bem, mas eles escolhem o Brasil pela fragilidade do nosso sistema de imigração e migração, do nosso sistema de registro de documento e da nossa rede pública de saúde", concluiu.

Mulheres tailandesas são suspeitas de vir ao Brasil para dar à luz e bebês seriam entregues a outras famílias mediante pagamento. — Foto: Polícia Civil

Após serem levados para a delegacia, Kelly Lee Squire e Qian Gao foram encaminhados ao sistema prisional, onde permaneceram à disposição da Justiça. Segundo a Polícia Civil, os bebês estão no hospital com acompanhamento das Assistentes Sociais do município de Saquarema aguardando decisão da Justiça. O g1 busca contato com a defesa dos suspeitos.

Polícia Civil pede que denúncias que contribuam com as investigações sejam repassadas, sob sigilo, ao Disque-Denúncia da 124ª Delegacia de Polícia pelo telefone (22) 99202-1973.

articles.title: Yaxley battery storage system could power 170,000 homes
articles.summary: Plans for the energy infrastructure are recommended for approval by the local council.
articles.body:
Plans to build a battery storage system capable of powering more than 170,000 homes have been recommended for approval.

CONNECTID 2 Ltd has applied to install the infrastructure on land west of the A140 at Red House Farm in Yaxley, near Eye, Suffolk.

However, the application has been opposed by Yaxley, Thrandeston and Mellis parish councils over concerns including flooding and fire safety.

Mid Suffolk District Council will make its final decision at a planning meeting on 2 December.

Blueprints showed the storage system would consist of 448 battery container units and be built on 10.4 hectares (25.7 acres) of mostly agricultural land.

The facilities enable electricity from renewable sources, such as solar and wind, to be stored outside of national and local networks and then released into the grid when power is required.

According to planning documents, the development would have 520MW of storage - enough energy to power 176,100 homes a day.

If permission is granted, the site will be returned to agricultural use after 40 years or if it goes six months without operating.

Similar proposals at land south of Eye Airfield Industrial Estate were approved by the council in July 2025.

The local authority is run by a Green, independent and Liberal Democrat coalition.

articles.title: Plans to be submitted for water park at Aberaeron farm shop
articles.summary: Developers also hope to build a wellness centre, fitness centre and spa.
articles.body:
Plans to build a water park on the site of an award-winning farm shop are set to be submitted.

The scheme at Moody Meadows near Aberaeron, Ceredigion, would also include a wellness centre, fitness centre and spa with accommodation.

Owners Chris and Geraint Thomas said the proposed development was now official after four years of planning.

A consultation will run until 20 December, with a formal application expected after that date.

Chris said the scheme would invest in the county and create jobs, giving tourism in Ceredigion the "top-quality destination" it deserves.

"It's a huge financial, emotional and personal price to pay to get this flagship development through planning and built, but with local suppliers, local craftsmen, local materials and local people – we wholeheartedly believe we can do this," she said.

The couple moved to the farm in 2010 after diversifying their cattle farm in the Bannau Brycheiniog national park, where they later lost everything because of legal problems.

They opened Bargoed Farm Campsite in 2018, using wooden hot tubs to attract visitors, before launching the Moody Cow Farm Shop and Welsh Kitchen, serving Welsh dishes made with local ingredients, and latterly Moody Meadows.

The attraction has since expanded, gaining permission for a trampoline park and, in 2023, permission to expand its caravan park.

Ceredigion council said the scale of the proposed development meant the applicants were required to carry out a pre-application consultation before a planning application could be submitted.

It said the council anticipated a planning application would be submitted in late December or January.

articles.title: Former Civil Nuclear Constabulary chief inspector jailed for rape
articles.summary: Glen Mahony once worked with Wayne Couzens, who was convicted of the 2021 murder of Sarah Everard.
articles.body:
A former police chief inspector who once worked with convicted murderer Wayne Couzens has been sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for two counts of rape and one of sexual assault.

Glen Mahony, 54, who was convicted at Maidstone Crown Court in September following a 10-day trial, carried out two attacks while his victim was asleep.

Mahony worked in the Civil Nuclear Constabulary (CNC) and previously worked with Couzens, who is serving a whole life tariff for the rape and murder of Sarah Everard in 2021.

In his sentencing remarks on Tuesday, Judge Gareth Branston dismissed Mahony's claims that he was targeted because he had once managed Couzens.

"You were not targeted. You were arrested because of what you did," he said.

He described Mahony's behaviour as "appalling", saying it had left his victim, who was known to him, suffering panic attacks and unable to work.

The judge said that when arrested in March 2022, Mahony told Kent Police officers that he had been Wayne Couzens's overall manager, though not his line manager.

The CNC, which guards the UK's nuclear facilities, is the force where Couzens served for six years before joining the Metropolitan Police.

Mahony, who was an inspector in charge of day-to-day police operations at the Dungeness power station before being promoted, was his commanding officer for some of that time.

Mahony was suspended on full pay by the CNC in March 2022 and resigned the day before a disciplinary hearing in January of this year.

The CNC said he would have been dismissed for gross misconduct if the disciplinary process had been carried out.

In an impact statement read to the court, his victim said she was made to feel worthless, and that "it was all about control for him".

"His actions didn't just hurt me at the time but have continued to do so each day. He has stolen my confidence," she said, having described ongoing nightmares and mental health struggles.

Det Ch Insp Tracy Evans, of Kent Police, said: "To take advantage of a woman while she is asleep and at her most vulnerable is utterly disgraceful and to then deny it happened and force the victim to relive her ordeal during a trial makes things even worse."

She also praised the "tremendous courage" of the victim in coming forward to report Mahony.

CNC Chief Constable Simon Chesterman said his immediate thoughts were with Mahony's victim, who he also commended for her bravery.

"Former officer Glen Mahony's crimes were despicable, committing the most serious sexual violence to a vulnerable female victim, who was not able to consent," he said.

"Mahony's behaviours are entirely contrary to the high standards required of a police officer with the CNC. And his actions go on to undermine the trust and confidence that the public, and particularly women, have in the police service."

Two WhatsApp groups to which Mahony belonged were also investigated by CNC professional standards.

"In these groups, Mahony sent sexist and misogynistic messages, and he did not challenge or leave the group when others sent similarly offensive messages," Chief Constable Chesterman said.

"This further underlines his disgusting opinion of women."

Mahony was promoted to chief inspector for the south division in 2020. It meant he was number three in the division's chain of command for the four nuclear sites in the south - Dungeness, Sizewell and Hinkley Point power stations, and the nuclear research centre at Harwell, Oxfordshire.

He spent most of his working life as an armed officer based at the Dungeness nuclear plant in Kent.

He joined the force in 2006, becoming a sergeant in 2011 before being promoted to inspector in 2016. This put him in operational charge of security at the site. He would have worked with Couzens, who was a constable at Dungeness between 2012 and 2018.

Couzens was also in a separate WhatsApp group with six other officers who transferred to the Met from the CNC. The messages they shared were found to be sexist, misogynistic, racist and violent, raising questions about the culture among officers at both the CNC and the Met.

articles.title: Five women killed every hour globally by partner, relative last year: UN
articles.summary: Home remains the most dangerous place for a woman or girl, ‘a pattern that has barely shifted in years’, UN Women says.
articles.body:
About 47,000 women and girls were killed intentionally by an intimate partner or family member last year, according to new data from the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and UN Women.

The 2026 Femicide Brief, published on Tuesday, marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

The report found that home remains the most dangerous place for a woman or girl, “a pattern that has barely shifted in years”, UN Women said in a statement.

About 60 percent of last year’s 78,000 femicides were committed by an intimate partner or family member. That amounts to five women being killed every hour, or 129 per day, on average.

While the 47,000 figure is lower than the 2024 estimate of 50,000 victims, this change is largely due to improvements and not indicative of an actual decrease, the UN statement said.

The femicides took place across the globe, with no region safe from such violence.

“Africa remains the continent with the highest rate of victims of intimate partner/family member femicide (2.9 victims per 100,000 female population), followed by the Americas (1.4 victims), Oceania (1.1 victims), Asia (0.6 victims), and Europe (0.5 victims),” UN Women said.

“For far too long, we have seen alarming statistics,” Executive Director of UNODC Monica Juma said in the statement. “Frightening attitudes, social norms, and the failure of institutional safeguards create an environment in which killing a wife, daughter, mother, or sister becomes ‘tolerable’.”

Juma called for action across all levels of society, including strategies targeted at changing societal behaviour and harmful attitudes, and investing in specialised programmes and interventions to “deal with perpetrators of domestic violence, protect women, and secure their human rights and dignity”.

Femicide is rarely an isolated act, but rather the final one in a long pattern of violence, threats, and abuse, said UN Women. Yet, most women and girls never seek help or are left without protection, while “perpetrators escape justice their entire lives”.

“We must ensure women can report violence safely, access protection, and receive support before it is too late,” said UN Women Executive Director Sima Bahous. “When warning signs go unreported, cases are not properly investigated, women and girls are not protected and perpetrators are not brought to justice, the consequences can be fatal.”

The UN has found that while homicide rates globally have declined, femicide rates have done so at a slower pace.

In fact, between 2010 and last year, homicide rates declined nearly twice as fast as femicide rates in the Americas, and about 1.5 times as fast in Europe.

articles.title: Palestine Weekly: A night of arson sees Israel ‘Jewish terrorism’ reckoning
articles.summary: Israeli settler pogroms have continued in the occupied West Bank.
articles.body:
Israeli settlers set fire to at least a dozen vehicles and several homes in five Palestinian villages across the occupied West Bank over the weekend, spray-painting “Revenge” and “Greetings from Susya”, apparently referring to the recent evacuation of an outpost near that village.

Police said they had opened investigations, according to local media, but no arrests have been reported.

In chat groups, settlers made light of the organised attacks, with one joking about the coming Jewish festival of lights: “Hanukkah is only in two weeks. We are in suspense.”

The attacks, part of a surge in settler violence against Palestinian villages, drew unusually sharp condemnation from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s political rivals. Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, seeking to form a new government, called them “Jewish terrorism in every sense of the word” and blamed far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.

Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett accused the government of enabling the attacks, with Yair Lapid calling them “pogroms”. The criticism came as Britain froze the assets of eight Israeli settlement firms and Australia imposed sanctions on settlers and their organisations.

Occupied West Bank: Arson and demolitions

Arson attacks restricted the olive harvest; according to the United Nations Humanitarian Country Team’s latest report, more than 400 attacks causing casualties or damage have occurred since September, including attacks against activists, journalists and diplomats.

Shootings and beatings: Settlers shot Asmat Tamimi in the abdomen while attacking olive pickers in Nabi Saleh on November 20, and beat farmer Mahmoud al-Harimi on his land in Abu Njeim on November 23, the Wafa news agency reported. During an olive harvest in Beitillu on November 20, settlers slashed the tyres of four cars of journalists. After soldiers forced pickers to leave the groves in Area B, settlers invaded the village, with troops using tear gas in the streets, according to witnesses and videos shared with Al Jazeera. Also on November 20, the Beit El illegal settlement’s civilian security coordinator shot dead Hamza Abdo, 42, near its perimeter wall.

Roads and sieges: Settlers attacked Palestinian vehicles on a near-daily basis on al-Mughayyir’s only access road, according to village council member Marzouq Abu Naim. On the night of November 22, settlers cut the village’s main power line and blocked its entrances under army protection. They also blocked roads in Burqa and Qabalan and pelted cars with stones near Efrat and on Route 60. On November 23, soldiers closed roads around Hebron with iron gates, concrete blocks and earth mounds. Hizma, northeast of Jerusalem, was sealed overnight on November 22 after soldiers fired live rounds at workers crossing the separation wall into Jerusalem, arresting 18, according to Israeli field monitor Jonathan Pollack.

Land, crops and water: Wafa and locals reported that settlers bulldozed dozens of olive trees in al-Mughayyir despite a court ruling allowing the owners back, destroyed about 70 trees in Aghziwa, burned groves in Burqa, ploughed 50 dunams in al-Farisiya and cut a water line in al-Masoudiya, where residents say they have been without electricity for two months. The UN’s Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs says more than 4,000 trees and saplings have been damaged this harvest season and over 25,000kg of produce vandalised or stolen.

Demolitions: Over the weekend, Israeli forces and Civil Administration officials demolished every structure at Khirbet Samra in the northern Jordan Valley, including water tanks that supplied its drinking water, according to Wafa and Pollack, who said more than 20 structures had no demolition orders and residents were given none. In Hebron, the army posted demolition notices on two Area A buildings containing 25 and 40 apartments, citing their proximity to a settler road. The Office of the State Attorney told Haaretz that the November 17 demolition of a home housing 32 people in Kafr ad-Dik, despite a High Court freeze, was “human error”.

Outposts: Haaretz reported that settlers built a yeshiva, a traditional Jewish educational institution, in Area A, meant to be under full Palestinian Authority (PA) control, in the village of Yasid, as a “satellite campus” to the Homesh outpost. Near Hebron, bulldozers began levelling land in Kharas for an industrial zone serving the Gush Etzion bloc after more than 500 dunams were declared a closed military zone.

Prisoners: A military judge upheld the administrative detention of Burin olive harvest and community organiser Ghassan Najjar, though the prosecutor acknowledged it was unrelated to armed activity. An Israeli court also extended the detention without charge of Gaza doctor Hussam Abu Safia by six months.

In Israel: On November 18, a Jewish driver rammed pedestrians at several locations in Kafr Qasim, wounding eight Palestinian citizens; police said there was no nationalist motive and the driver tested positive for drugs. On November 19, masked men set fire to a mosque in Ed-Dahi and left graffiti about revenge for a settler killed in March, according to The Times of Israel.

Gaza: Killings continue as health crisis deepens

The Gaza Ministry of Health’s death toll since the October 2025 “ceasefire” rose from 1,650 on November 16 to 1,679 on November 23, bringing the number of deaths in the genocidal war since October 2023 to 74,746. On November 18, Israeli tanks and bulldozers crossed the “Yellow Line” in central Gaza in the first publicly announced ground push since the “ceasefire”.

The army said it was destroying a tunnel; about 6,000 people fled ad-Dawa, Bureij and Nuseirat, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office. Troops withdrew the next day. A Palestinian security source told Al Jazeera that Israeli-backed anti-Hamas groups helped pressure families to leave.

Killings: On November 21, a drone strike hit a van carrying meals from a charity kitchen in Tal al-Hawa, Gaza City, killing three people. The Israeli army claimed they were members of Islamic Jihad, but a witness told the Reuters news agency the van was about to stop to give food to children. On November 20, drones killed at least seven people in central Gaza, including four friends in Bureij who the army said were Hamas operatives planning attacks. Six-year-old Iyas al-Namnam was shot dead east of Deir el-Balah on November 17. The army told The Times of Israel it was not aware of the incident.

Demolitions: Maghazi Mayor Mohammed Musleh said more than 500 housing units had been destroyed “in less than a month”, describing it as gradual displacement, as hundreds of displaced people protested near the “Yellow Line” in Deir el-Balah on November 21.

Disease and shortages: On November 22, the Gaza Health Ministry warned of an out-of-season rise in meningitis linked to damaged sewage networks. Al-Shifa hospital’s director said 12 people have died so far from the disease, and that medical gowns and fabrics have run out in every hospital, threatening surgery. On November 23, a child died from lead poisoning, which was blamed on Israel’s ban on new batteries, forcing families to repair old ones inside tents.

Aid and evacuations: The Beit Hanoon crossing, known as Erez to Israelis, reopened for aid screening on November 18 for the first time since February 2025, allowing about 20 trucks a day. But five aid groups gave a score of four out of 26 to United States President Donald Trump’s peace plan in Gaza, saying it failed to deliver adequate aid, protection, freedom of movement, reconstruction or economic revival. Amid mounting international criticism, the Trump-appointed Board of Peace warned the UN Security Council that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely”.

The arsons in the occupied West Bank struck a nerve amid Israeli coalition negotiations. Ben-Gvir called Eisenkot’s condemnation of the attacks a “down payment” to MK Ahmad Tibi, leader of the Arab Ta’al party, according to The Times of Israel. Yesha Council chair Israel Ganz condemned the arson but said the term “Jewish terrorism” served those seeking to tarnish Israel. Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned “a handful of extremists” but promised countermeasures following the British and Australian sanctions.

Meanwhile, Israel’s left-leaning attorney general froze the E1 settlement tender until a new government is sworn in.

Netanyahu’s Likud party and Eisenkot’s Yashar ended coalition talks without a deal on November 22 over who would lead the country and whether Ben-Gvir would join the new government.

Eisenkot indicated to Israeli media that if a broad coalition fails, he may rely on outside support from Joint List and Ra’am, the two Arab parties whose potential support Netanyahu has repeatedly demonised during negotiations, to form a minority government.

articles.title: South African court convicts Zimbabwean of trying to fight in Russia-Ukraine war
articles.summary: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
articles.body:
A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine.

The country has strict laws which restrict unauthorised involvement in overseas wars.

Twenty-four-year-old Wesley Sothole, who pleaded guilty, was handed a five-year suspended prison sentence and was ordered to be deported from South Africa.

He is one of five Zimbabweans who were arrested at OR Tambo Airport in Johannesburg on 8 November. South African prosecutors have not confirmed which side the Zimbabweans allegedly intended to fight for.

Sothole's four co-accused have yet to enter pleas and are due to return to the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court on 1 December for further plea and sentencing proceedings.

Another four Zimbabweans were arrested at a hotel in Johannesburg at the same time in a joint operation and are facing a different court process.

The investigation has involved South African police, Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies.

South Africa's Foreign Military Assistance Act was passed in 1998 at a time when the government was concerned about members of the former apartheid security services going to fight elsewhere in Africa.

There has been growing concern across Africa over the recruitment of its citizens to fight in the war in Ukraine, with some reportedly being lured to Russia by promises of lucrative civilian employment.

A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia.

Some have been captured and are being held as prisoners of war.

In March, Kenya estimated that 252 of its citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia.

Kenyan Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue. He said an agreement had been reached for Russia to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals.

In the same month, Zimbabwe said that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines.

The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 of its nationals who were allegedly tricked into joining the war.

In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war.

South Africa's government said it condemned "the exploitation of young vulnerable people by individuals working with foreign military entities".

Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa.

articles.body: Passengers aboard a morning flight out of Boston faced an unusual pause on the tarmac recently after a four-legged traveler broke free in the cabin. articles.summary: MacKenzie Scott, the ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who has sold around half of her Amazon shares, donated $62 million to marine conservation
articles.body: MacKenzie Scott, the ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who has sold around half of her Amazon shares, donated $62 million to marine conservation organisation Blue Ventures. The contribution, described by the organisation as a “landmark gift”, will support small-scale fishing communities across tropical regions and help them protect marine ecosystems and livelihoods. The funding will also support Blue Ventures' ambitious 2030 goals, which include enabling 10,000 fishing communities to lead marine conservation efforts, improving food security and economic resilience for 5 million people, and bringing 200,000 square kilometres of carbon-rich seas under local stewardship.Why MacKenzie Scott donated $62 million to Blue VenturesThe donation, announced in December 2025, comes at a time when coastal communities are facing growing challenges from warming seas, declining fish catches and climate change. According to Blue Ventures, more than 100 million people depend on small-scale fishing for their daily food and livelihood. The organisation said the gift recognises the leadership of coastal communities and the solutions they are already developing using local knowledge and experience.Blue Ventures CEO Ebrima Saidy said: “This gift strengthens trust in community-led conservation at a moment when coastal communities are carrying the greatest burden of the climate and ocean crisis. It enables us to continue standing firmly beside communities, complementing their efforts and respecting their autonomy to lead effectively. By backing approaches that have been shaped and proven locally, this funding helps fishing communities continue to safeguard marine life, sustain their way of life, and better respond to the challenges of a changing climate”.What are Blue Ventures' 2030 goalsAs stated above, Mackenzie Scott’s $62 million contribution will support the organisation's 2030 strategy, which places community leadership at the centre of marine conservation. Its targets include:Enabling 10,000 fishing communities to lead fisheries management and marine conservation.Improving food security and economic resilience for 5 million people.Bringing 200,000 square kilometres of carbon-rich seas under effective local stewardship.Equipping hundreds of grassroots organisations and communities with funding, skills, data and advocacy support.A significant proportion of the funding will go directly to local partners through the Frontline Community Fund, providing flexible, long-term resources for communities to set their own priorities.Chelsea Wieber, Blue Ventures' Director of Development, said: “This generous award couldn’t come at a more important moment for climate action and community-led solutions. We’re grateful for the trust and flexibility this funding brings, supporting not just our work but many others striving for a healthier, more resilient planet. articles.title: A Michigan physician missed a required divorce hearing to catch a work flight after 19 years of marriage; an appeals court upheld his default but threw out support orders lacking evidence of either spouse's income
articles.summary: A work flight took priority over a court appearance, but the decision came with significant legal consequences.
articles.body: A work flight took priority over a court appearance, but the decision came with significant legal consequences. A Michigan physician who missed a mandatory divorce hearing after being instructed repeatedly to attend in person has lost his challenge against a default judgment. However, while the appeals court upheld the decision to hold him in default, it found that major financial and child custody arrangements in the divorce were made without sufficient evidence, sending those matters back for further proceedings.After 19 years of marriage, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed and reversed Paula Clare Ma and Marcus Ma's divorce judgment on November 20, 2026.Doctor lost hearing after multiple warningsPaula Ma filed for divorce from Marcus after nearly 20 years, according to the Michigan Court of Appeals. Marcus worked as a travelling physician, a professional commitment that became central to the dispute over his failure to attend court proceedings.Marcus was found in default for missing a mediation and pretrial conference in May 2025.He missed a second pretrial conference on February 27, 2026, despite the parties' agreement to vacate that default.The appeals court noted that the February hearing date had been arranged in December 2025, when both spouses were present. Marcus had personally agreed to the date, and the court subsequently issued an order requiring both parties and their lawyers to attend in person.Despite these instructions, Marcus contacted court staff shortly before the hearing, requesting an adjournment because he needed to travel out of town for work.Court rejected physician's explanationThe Michigan Court of Appeals found that Marcus had been repeatedly informed that his presence was mandatory. Both his attorney and court staff had made clear that the hearing would not be postponed.Nevertheless, Marcus emailed the court on the morning of February 27, indicating that he was boarding a plane and would be unable to attend.He later argued that his professional responsibilities provided a reasonable explanation for his absence. He also questioned why his lawyer had not successfully sought an adjournment on his behalf.However, the appeals court concluded that his circumstances did not amount to sufficient grounds for overturning the default. The judges highlighted that he had knowingly disregarded the court's instructions and was already aware that another default could be entered following his earlier absence. The court therefore upheld the lower court's refusal to set aside the default judgment.Financial orders overturned over missing income evidenceWhile the physician failed to overturn the default, the appeals court identified serious shortcomings in how the lower court determined the financial arrangements between the former spouses.According to the Michigan Court of Appeals, the trial court had ordered Marcus to pay spousal support for 10 years and had also imposed child support obligations without receiving evidence establishing either parent's income.The judges found that the trial court had failed to provide the factual findings necessary to justify these financial decisions.The appeals court also addressed the decision to make spousal support nonmodifiable. It noted that Michigan law generally allows either party to request a modification of spousal support, unless the statutory right has been waived. There was no indication that either spouse had agreed to waive that right.Consequently, the spousal support provision and the accompanying support order were vacated for reconsideration.The child support order was also overturned because the lower court had not established the parents' respective incomes or demonstrated that its calculation followed the Michigan Child Support Formula.Children's schooling and custody arrangements sent backThe appeals court further questioned the lower court's handling of arrangements concerning the couple's four minor children.The original judgment included provisions for joint legal and physical custody, parenting time and the children's school district. However, the Michigan Court of Appeals found that the trial court had not properly assessed the children's best interests before making these decisions.The only evidence presented on the issue was the wife's brief testimony supporting the proposed arrangements. The lower court had not examined whether an established custodial environment existed with either parent or made findings based on Michigan's statutory best-interest factors. The appeals court therefore vacated the custody and parenting-time provisions as well.On remand, the trial court must reconsider the children's best interests, including whether remaining in their existing school district would serve their welfare.The ruling leaves the default judgment intact but requires a fresh examination of crucial financial and family arrangements, highlighting that a party's failure to attend divorce proceedings does not eliminate the court's obligation to establish evidence-based decisions.Image Courtesy: Google GeminiYou use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk donated nearly $500,000 to Flint schools in 2018 after an X user challenged him to help the city; the contribution supported plans for water filtration systems across 12 school buildings
articles.summary: An X post exchange in July 2018 led to a donation that would help address a persistent problem in Flint, Michigan, where years of water contamination had
articles.body: An X post exchange in July 2018 led to a donation that would help address a persistent problem in Flint, Michigan, where years of water contamination had left residents wary of using ordinary taps and drinking fountains. Elon Musk, who had publicly responded to a resident asking him to help the city, eventually committed financial support through his foundation. As reported by Fortune, by October, Flint Community Schools had confirmed a contribution of $480,350 to install water filtration equipment across its buildings. The initiative covered 12 school buildings and the district headquarters, with the aim of giving students access to treated drinking water without relying on bottled supplies.Elon Musk pledged nearly $500,000 for Flint school water filtersThe sequence began on July 11, 2018, when Musk responded to an X (Formerly Twitter) user who challenged him to help Flint. The exchange was brief, but the Tesla chief executive did not leave the offer at the level of an online response. His initial involvement included offering assistance to residents who had received concerning water test results, including helping arrange individual water filter installations.The support eventually extended beyond individual households. In an X (Formerly Twitter) post on October 5, 2018, Flint Community Schools announced that Musk and the Musk Foundation had pledged nearly $480,350 towards installing ultraviolet filtration systems throughout the district. The announcement followed months of public attention surrounding the city's continuing efforts to address the effects of contaminated water.Musk also responded when the school district publicly acknowledged the contribution. He indicated that he hoped to provide further assistance in the future.What the filtration project was expected to coverReportedly, the proposed installation programme included all 12 buildings operated by Flint Community Schools, along with the district's administrative headquarters. The equipment was expected to be in place by January 2019.The filtration systems were intended to address both lead contamination and bacterial concerns. While the filtration technology would remove lead from drinking water, ultraviolet treatment would help disinfect the supply by targeting bacteria. The installations were expected to allow students and staff to use school drinking fountains and refill their bottles.Flint Community Schools Superintendent Derrick Lopez said, “We are deeply grateful for the generosity and the budding partnership between Flint Community Schools, the Musk Foundation and Elon Musk. The new water filtration systems will be instrumental in helping our students return to the normalcy of what should be a fundamental right: having access to safe, clean water from water fountains in their school.”Why Flint continued to face concerns about its waterThe donation came against the background of a crisis that had affected Flint since 2014. The city's decision to change its water source was made while it was under state-appointed emergency management, with reducing expenses among the considerations. The new supply was not adequately treated with corrosion-control chemicals, allowing lead from ageing pipes and plumbing infrastructure to enter the water.The consequences extended beyond household taps. Residents reported concerns about the colour and quality of their water, while testing revealed dangerous lead contamination. An outbreak of Legionnaires' disease was also linked to the water-source change, adding another dimension to the public health emergency.Flint is a predominantly Black city that had already experienced decades of economic decline following the contraction of General Motors' operations in the area. The water emergency unfolded amid these existing financial and administrative difficulties, eventually becoming a major dispute over public health, government accountability and the management of essential services.Although problems were apparent in 2014, the response developed slowly. Michigan Governor Rick Snyder declared a state of emergency in Flint's county in January 2016, as pressure mounted over the handling of the contamination.Flint's water improvements left concerns over lead in schools and homesBy 2018, work was under way to replace thousands of lead-containing service lines across the city. However, the process was expected to continue for years, with the replacement programme unlikely to be completed before at least 2020.State authorities had reported that water quality had improved, and testing conducted from early 2017 indicated lower lead levels. Yet concerns remained, particularly in schools, where some water samples continued to exceed recommended safety thresholds.The research published in American Journal of Public Health (AJPH), titled, ‘Elevated Blood Lead Levels in Children Associated With the Flint Drinking Water Crisis: A Spatial Analysis of Risk and Public Health Response’, where flint paediatrician Dr Mona Hanna-Attisha, played an important role in bringing the contamination to wider public attention, continued to advise people to use bottled or properly filtered water. Pipe replacement itself could disturb accumulated material and release lead into the supply, making caution necessary even as infrastructure work progressed.The wider response to the Flint crisisThe water emergency also triggered investigations into decisions made by officials responsible for the city's water system. Several local and state officials faced criminal charges connected to the crisis, including allegations involving misconduct and involuntary manslaughter. The cases formed part of a broader examination of how the water-source switch was approved and why corrosion controls were not properly implemented.Musk's contribution arrived while the city was still dealing with the practical consequences of those decisions. His donation was directed towards a defined need within the school district, rather than the complete replacement of Flint's ageing water infrastructure.At the time, Musk was also facing considerable scrutiny over his public statements and his dispute with the US Securities and Exchange Commission concerning tweets about potentially taking Tesla private. The Flint announcement received attention amid those developments, though the school district's filtration project had its own timetable and purpose.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Global landmine casualties hit a five-year high, driven by Myanmar, Syria
articles.summary: Landmine monitor found 84 percent of deaths caused by landmines were in Southeast Asia.
articles.body:
Casualties from landmines or unexploded ordnance reached a five-year high in 2025, with the largest number of deaths recorded in Southeast Asia, largely driven by Myanmar’s civil war.

A report by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines found civilians were the most affected, making up some 84 percent of the 6,929 casualties recorded in 2025, half of them were children.

In Myanmar, where both the government and armed groups are using landmines, 1,891 deaths were recorded in 2025, the highest number of any country for the third consecutive year.

On average, five people are killed or wounded by landmines daily in Myanmar, the report found.

“Myanmar has gone beyond crisis to catastrophe, and has claimed the ignoble title of top producer of landmine victims for a third year in a row,” said Yeshua Moser-Puangsuwan, a co-author of the Landmine Monitor 2026 report.

“There is now contamination at some level in almost two-thirds of the townships of the country.”

Myanmar – along with Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and other countries in the region – accounted for 27 percent of global deaths from landmines in 2025, despite having only 8 percent of the world’s population.

Syria saw a spike of more than 50 percent in casualties, with 1,602 deaths recorded in 2025 after large numbers of civilians returned after the fall of ousted President Bashar al-Assad in 2024.

“Syria is huge, but it is a post-war crisis,” Moser-Puangsuwan said. “People are now returning, and that is driving the casualty figure. They need to radically scale up their clearance capacity.”

Five European countries opted out of Mine Ban Treaty

The International Campaign to Ban Landmines has been urging more countries to join the 1997 Mine Ban Treaty to end stockpiling, production and the transfer of antipersonnel mines.

Despite this, five countries on the borders with Russia – Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland – pulled out of the treaty, citing the “security situation in our region”.

Ukraine, meanwhile, notified the United Nations that it had decided to suspend the implementation of the treaty, even though such a move is not allowed under its provisions.

Russia, not a party to the treaty, has been making widespread use of mines in its invasion of Ukraine, and Landmine Monitor found that Ukraine had been using them as well.

Lebanon, the Marshall Islands and Tonga all joined the Mine Ban Treaty during the reporting period, and 162 countries are now bound by it.

articles.title: A Philadelphia woman said she had occupied an abandoned house since 2003 and sought ownership by adverse possession; after a 23-year claim, a Pennsylvania appeals court dismissed her case over filing defects
articles.summary: The Pennsylvania Superior Court on Friday dismissed a womans attempt to claim ownership of a house she said she had occupied since 2003 Diana R.
articles.body: The Pennsylvania Superior Court on Friday dismissed a womans attempt to claim ownership of a house she said she had occupied since 2003Diana R. Garner claimed she had found the house at 2706 West George Street abandoned and had occupied it for nearly 23 years. She approached the court seeking legal ownership, but the property had been in the name of Scott Mendelsohn, associated with Tyson Realty, since 2017.The dispute first went before a Philadelphia County court, which ruled in Mendelsohn's favour in January. Garner challenged that decision before the state's Superior Court, arguing that the lower court had failed to properly consider her claim and the time she had spent at the property.But the appeals court did not take up the ownership dispute for a detailed review. It found that Garner's appeal lacked the legal material needed to examine her objections and dismissed it.How the ownership dispute unfoldedAccording to the case details available on Justia, Garner's case centred on her claim that she had occupied the property after finding it abandoned around 2003. The property owner challenged her complaint, prompting the trial court to ask Garner to submit a revised version of her case within 20 days in October 2025. She missed that deadline.Mendelsohn subsequently asked the court to rule in his favour. Garner did not respond to his request before the trial court granted it in January.She submitted a revised complaint, but it was late and had not been filed with the court's permission. She later argued that an earlier electronic submission had been rejected because a required document was missing. However, the appeals court noted that even the earlier date she cited would have fallen outside the deadline.Garner then challenged the January ruling, maintaining that the court should have considered her claims instead of ending the case over procedural issues.Why the appeals court rejected her caseThe main problem with Garner's appeal was the way she presented her arguments. The judges found that her written submission did not contain proper legal references to support her objections.She argued that there were unresolved questions about how long she had occupied and used the property. She also questioned the trial court's decision to rule in Mendelsohn's favour without a response from her.However, the appeals court said she had not explained these claims with sufficient legal support. Her submission also lacked references to the court records that could have helped establish the basis for her arguments.The judges noted that Garner had listed some legal cases and court rules in the reference section of her submission. But the cases were not discussed in her arguments. The court was also unable to locate the two cases using the details she had provided.Garner represented herself during the proceedings. The judges acknowledged that courts can take a more flexible approach when dealing with people who do not have lawyers. However, they said this did not mean the court could prepare legal arguments on an appellant's behalf.The Superior Court concluded that the gaps in her submission made it impossible to properly review her complaints. It therefore dismissed the appeal.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Benjamin Franklin impersonator arrested in Boston while still in costume
articles.summary: A man dressed in a full Benjamin Franklin outfit was arrested by police in Boston’s North End on Monday afternoon.
articles.body: A man dressed in a full Benjamin Franklin outfit was arrested by police in Boston’s North End on Monday afternoon. Boston police said some of their officers were conducting a coordinated warrant sweep and crime prevention operation in downtown Boston when around 2:15 p.m. they noticed a man dressed head to toe as Benjamin Franklin on Hanover Street. Upon closer inspection, police said they recognized the man “not as the Founding Father” but as 66-year-old Timothy Kingman, of Beacon Hill, who was wanted on two active warrants. Officers approached him, informed him of the warrants and arrested him. He was wanted on warrants for shoplifting and assault and battery out of Boston Municipal Court, police said. An onlooker captured the whole incident on video, which shows two plainclothes officers handcuffing the costumed character. Kingman was taken to the Nashua Street Jail for booking, police said, and he was arraigned in Boston Municipal Court on Tuesday morning, still wearing his colonial garb. Prosecutors asked for $500 cash bail on the assault charge, while defense attorney Nicholas Santiago asked that Kingman be released on personal recognizance, which the judge granted. Santiago said Kingman is a Benjamin Franklin impersonator and it’s something he’s passionate about. He said Kingman has run his own business doing tours in Boston for the past six years. Before that, he said Kingman had a long history of employment as an electrician and served in the Coast Guard for eight years. “He is truly dedicated to service and working, and that’s something he would continue to do if released,” Santiago said. The attorney also pointed out that the incident that led to the assault charge involved Kingman having his phone knocked from his hand and suffering shoulder and thumb injuries that required treatment. The alleged victim suffered no injuries, he said. Santiago said the altercation stemmed from his client’s issues with alcohol and that he’s been sober ever since. The police report said the incident, which occurred on March 2, involved a dispute between Kingman and another person who was conducting a tour of the Freedom Trail for a group of students. The victim told police that Kingman appeared intoxicated, interrupting him and shoving him several times and swinging at him. He then followed and verbally harassed the group, eventually leaving the area only when a security guard at Faneuil Hall intervened. Kingman is scheduled to return to court on Jan. 13, 2027, for a pretrial hearing.

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.summary: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.
articles.body:
Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark trial in the US.

In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.

Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.

In a statement, Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years".

Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which also included conspiracy to violate US sanctions.

However the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise.

Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019, after the dramatic arrest in late 2018 of senior executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada.

Meng, also known as Cathy Meng, was held for three years in Canada before she was released to return to China through a deal with US prosecutors.

During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms to ensure it had a competitive edge.

The BBC contacted the US Department of Justice for comment.

However, defence attorney Brian Heberlig said Huawei had grown into business with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff through hard work.

Following the verdict, Heberlig told the BBC that Huawei was gratified the jury had rejected the racketeering charge.

"The RICO count that alleged that Huawei was a corrupt organisation, with a corporate culture and policy of committing crime. That was, in our view, a significant overreach, and the jury soundly rejected it," he said.

"Of course, we have mixed emotions about the rest of the verdict ... [we] thought that Huawei was deserving of acquittals across the board."

Sentencing is planned for September 2027. Heberlig said there will be "significant advocacy" to achieve the lowest sentence possible. Following that, he said he fully expects Huawei to appeal.

"If I know Huawei, that fight will continue, and the company's not going to rest until it's pursued every last argument it can through appeal, and hopefully, ultimately toward vindication," he said.
